intro: Paying people and suppliers: asking to pay, the people you pay, payments in batches, repeating payments, and expenses to approve and repay.
start: Add the people you pay in Beneficiaries, and have their accounts approved.
Ask to pay someone in Payment requests; it goes for approval before money moves.

articles.title: Ask to pay someone, and get it approved
articles.summary: Write a payment request for a supplier's invoices or anything else, have it approved, then pay it now, on a date, or by hand.
before: The person you pay needs an approved account in Beneficiaries.

steps.rest: on Payment requests.

steps.lead: Choose what it is for and who it goes to.
steps.rest: For a supplier, tick the invoices still owed and say how much each one settles, withholds or takes as a discount.
their account, the way it is paid, and the account it leaves. What is paid is worked out for you.
If it looks like a payment already asked for, say why it is not a duplicate. You never approve your own request.
Pay now, Pay on a date…, or Record as paid by hand with the bank's reference.
for a payment made by hand. Someone other than whoever recorded it confirms it.

articles.after: Paid, it is settled in the books and the person paid is emailed a remittance advice.
tips: If the payment gives no answer, it shows as unknown. Press Verify with the provider: it is never sent twice.
Money the bank sends back? Press It came back. The invoices are owed again.

articles.title: Add someone you pay, and their bank account
articles.summary: Save a supplier, member of staff or anyone else you pay, with an account checked with the bank and approved before it is used.

steps.rest: and choose the kind and who it is, or type a name for someone else.
on the beneficiary, and enter the bank and account number.
The name the bank holds is shown beside the name you gave.
If the names differ, or no bank could check it, say why. It is paid only once it is approved.

tips: An account is never edited. Use Change to another account; the old one retires when the new one is approved.
Only the last four digits are shown, unless you have permission to see the whole number.

articles.title: Pay many approved payments in one run
articles.summary: Put approved payments from one account into a batch, have it approved once, and pay it or write the bank file.

steps.rest: on Payment batches. Give it a name and choose how it is paid.
They are grouped by the account they are paid from, and the total adds up as you tick.
The run is approved once, by someone other than you.
or Write the bank file to upload at your bank yourself.

steps.lead: Mark each line Paid or Not paid
steps.rest: as the bank reports, or press All paid, as the bank reports.

tips: To pay suppliers' bills straight from what is due, press Pay bills and tick the bills.
Before anything is paid, Call it off frees its payments again.

articles.title: Pay rent or a subscription every month
articles.summary: A recurring payment raises a payment request ahead of each date, approved once as a standing order.

steps.rest: on Recurring payments.

steps.lead: Choose the beneficiary, what it is for and the amount,
steps.rest: with the account it is paid from and how.
every month on a day, from a start date, and when it ends. The next dates are shown before you save.
leave each request for review, submit it, or carry it through under this approval.
Once approved, it raises a request on each date, once.

tips: Pause it, Skip the next date or End it from its page. Changing the amount or dates sends it back for approval.
All recurring shows every repeating payment, invoice and bill, and What falls when shows them month by month.

articles.title: Approve a staff expense claim and pay it back
articles.summary: Approve or send back what staff spent for the business. Approved, it is booked and the person is repaid through a payment request.
before: Set your categories and policies on the Categories and policies tab: the expense account each posts to, limits, and when a receipt is needed.

steps.rest: and open a claim. You see each line, its receipt, and anything past the policy.
and choose Approve, or Send back with why. You never approve your own claim.

steps.lead: Approved, it is posted to the books
steps.rest: and what the person is owed becomes a payment request to repay them.
if the claim is waiting, for example because the person had no approved account yet.

articles.after: When the payment request is paid, the claim shows as reimbursed.
tips: Staff make claims from My expenses › New claim.
Cash advances are on their own tab: approve, issue, and record cash handed back.
